correctness.rationale: The proof explicitly defines the 15 duads, 15 synthemes and induced edges. For each chosen duad set S, private-syntheme choices are independent and counted by a product, with a bijection proving no overcount. The analytical injection into disjoint pairs of complement K6-edges bounds size by nine and forces the complement to be two triangles at equality; it establishes the ten balanced-partition optima. Distinct optima overlap in at most five edges, and the independently checked coefficient 90 at size eight proves unique completion. Two standalone exact algorithms independently enumerate all 54866 matchings, all coefficients and maximal-set counts; each consumes the complete certificate files and checks them. Both executed successfully from their actual source files; no infinite or other-graph claim is inferred from finite enumeration.

originality.rationale: Primary full-text comparison with Cimráková–Fack (2007) finds point-only partial ovoids and line-only partial spreads, neither a flag induced-matching polynomial nor a saturation classification. Full-text comparison with Balasubramanian (2025) finds the ordinary matching polynomial: its two-edge coefficient 900 exceeds the induced two-edge coefficient 720, so its table does not contain the present invariant. Search queries used both induced/strong matching and duad–syntheme aliases. The new assertion additionally includes a separate ten-optimum 3+3-partition bijection and a unique size-eight completion theorem. Published-record search revealed no stronger matching statement or table covering these claims; absolute priority remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed table, historical graph census, or specialist generalized-quadrangle classification could contain the same induced-matching polynomial or saturation results.

value.rationale: The natural 30-vertex incidence graph of the smallest thick generalized quadrangle has a complete strong-matching census and a structurally unexpected saturation gap: maximal sizes 5,6,7,9 but none at eight. All ninety size-eight strong matchings uniquely complete to the ten optima, classified geometrically by balanced partitions. The precise all-size polynomial and optima classification are useful benchmarks distinct from the published ordinary-matching polynomial; the value is the geometric rigidity and unique completion, not a routine substitution of a numeric invariant.
